title: How Funstra is made
stamp: Development process · One loop per demo
tagline: One creative director agent, four reviewer agents, and a pipeline that publishes whatever survives. This is the whole loop, in the order it actually runs.
lede: Funstra is not written in one pass and reviewed afterwards. Each demo is a full turn around a three-phase loop: the director builds, the panel plays and tears it apart, the director integrates what was worth integrating. Only then does a release reach the website. Publication ends the cycle; the product owner then chooses whether to continue or change direction.

phases.title: The director takes a turn at the game
phases.kicker: Ends when a demo builds and passes the harness
phases.body: The director reads the documentation map in README, the game promise in VISION, the setting in WORLD and the single development plan in DESIGN. GitHub issues own execution status. A planning-only request ends with docs and tickets; a development cycle delivers the next coherent playable release.
points: It may employ subagents. Implementation, art passes, harness work and investigation can each be handed to a subagent working to a written brief.
It plans the issues and the demo release — what ships in this turn, what is explicitly out of scope, and what the panel is being asked to judge.
It can also just do the work. Delegation is a tool, not a rule; small turns are often faster written directly.
The turn ends at a real executable. Nothing goes to review until the rules harness and the runtime harness both pass on a built player.

Space is gameplay. New neighborhoods need distinct routes, useful thresholds, visible work and shared player/NPC interaction rules. The six-release arc in DESIGN is future intent, reviewed after each demo.

phases.title: The demo goes to the panel
phases.kicker: Triggered once the demo is done · all four run
phases.body: Four reviewer agents assess the current game and the committed demo through guided runs of its actual executable, screenshots and logs, with the manual and source available for inspection. Each reports Game now, Slice delivery and Evidence coverage separately. Fixed category weights preserve distinct priorities; agreement and disagreement are both allowed, never manufactured.
points: Each files a numerical ledger. Game now rates current quality and completeness; Slice delivery measures weighted release commitments. Missing outcomes lose explicit points, with caps for unavailable core experiences and unrecoverable progress loss. Evidence coverage identifies what was actually resolved; guided runs are not exploratory play.

One dossier per demo brings together the four reviews, their conference and the director’s disposition. Follow-up fixes and replays update that same case file; earlier demos keep their original dossiers.

Progress stays auditable. Reviews show comparable category changes, major remaining shortcomings and evidence limits. Historical reviews and scores remain unedited; the new rubric starts a separately labelled baseline.

They judge independently across the full 0–10 scale. No default 7, target 8 or persona floor. A passing small slice does not establish a complete game, and calling a missing experience future work does not restore its points.

phases.title: Integration, then the final release
phases.kicker: Closes the turn · publishes to the website
phases.body: The director reads all four reviews and decides what they change. This is a judgement step, not a checklist: bugs are not optional, but taste notes are weighed against the vision and some are declined on the record.
points: Bugs get fixed. Anything the panel hit that breaks the build, the rules or the fiction is repaired before release.
Feedback deemed worthy gets integrated — the notes that make the demo more of what it is trying to be, not merely more agreeable.
The rest is answered, not silently dropped. Declined feedback is recorded with a reason and often shows up as a later demo's premise.
A final release ships. One command builds, verifies, zips, hashes and publishes it, and the site regenerates itself from the release list.

loopNote: Publishing closes this cycle. The director reports the release and remaining tickets, then stops for the product owner to continue or change direction. GitHub and the website retain the latest five published demos (all available while fewer than five exist). Previous versions remain linked on the download page; older release assets are removed, while source tags and review records remain. Maintain one document per subject: do not create parallel roadmaps. Historical guides, validation and review records retain their build identity. Owner acceptance is separate from panel scores and publication.
reviewersNote: Evaluation protocol v2 and the fixed weights live in reviewer-agents/README.md. The five game categories are systems, people, control and comfort, craft and reliability, and sustained play. Each profile weights them differently. Reviews publish credit, deductions, caps and uncertainty instead of treating a clean harness run as an 8. Original reviews retain their original scoring context.

artefacts.desc: A written demo premise: what this turn is for, and what is out of scope.
A Windows player built in batch mode and validated by the rules and runtime harnesses.
Four independent guided reviews with separate game and slice ratings, numerical ledgers and evidence coverage, preserved unedited in reviewer-agents/.
One case file per demo combining all four reviews, the conference, director decisions and later replay findings.
Per-reviewer meeting memory carried into the next demo's review.
Bug repairs and the integrated share of the feedback, with declines recorded.
A tagged GitHub Release with notes and a SHA-256, which redeploys this site automatically.
